question.problem: In a right triangle $△OMN,$ $∠M$ is a right angle, $MN=1.8$ and $ON=3.$ Determine $\operatorname{cos}⁡O.$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/5c980bff90a516627618909a863b4919dbb10be1b674911cae663f3f7c54f3fb.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡O=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{OM}{ON}=\frac{OM}{3}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing side $OM.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}OM & =\sqrt{O{N}^{2}-M{N}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}-{1.8}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9-3.24} \\  & =\sqrt{5.76} \\  & =2.4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡O & =\frac{OM}{3} \\  & =\frac{2.4}{3} \\  & =\frac{24}{30} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
